frontier.hypothesis: The Y2b/Y4 parameter split is one insn from distance 0: a spelling that keeps a4's and pa4's reference sets apart WITHOUT materialising `addu $s7,$v0,$zero` gives ALL-TARGET seats plus target's block-2 addiu at 132 insns.
frontier.mechanism: The copy exists only because a4 becomes a block-0-LOCAL quantity (its last use is the copy itself), so local_alloc assigns it a call-clobbered register before global_alloc seats pa4, and GCC 2.7 never coalesces a local quantity into a global allocno. Anything that makes a4 and pa4 share one hard register -- or that removes one pa4 reference so the wrap's +1 nets back to 7 without splitting at all -- removes the insn.
frontier.next_probe: Two spellings to measure on Y4: (a) give a4 a use in a LATER block so it becomes a global allocno and global.c's copy preference can seat it in $s7 (watch whether it then steals a seat and spills a3, as the s19 uservar copy did); (b) enumerate whether any ONE of pa4's seven references can be re-sourced through out2 or out3 without changing emitted bytes -- pa4 at 7 refs with the wrap's +1 is exactly the 1473 the seat order wants.
